pipeline: domain_classifier (routing) + per-domain logistic-regression specialists on CLIP pre-projection features EXTENDED with a jpeg_q50 reactivity-delta feature, confidence-gated (soft mixture-of-experts) inference
backbone_feature_used: pre-projection embedding (768-dim vision-encoder pooled output, before visual_projection) CONCATENATED with the embedding shift caused by re-JPEG-compressing the image at quality 50 (768-dim delta) = 1536-dim total. See 'Reactivity-delta feature' in README - validated via diagnostic_reactivity_delta.py / diagnostic_reactivity_comprehensive.py / prelim_integration_test.py / prelim_domain_matched_probe.py before production integration (train_reactivity_specialists.py).
domain_classifier: RandomForestClassifier on classical no-reference features (laplacian_var, highfreq_ratio, blockiness, contrast, mean_saturation)
specialist_heads: sklearn Pipeline(StandardScaler, LogisticRegression) per domain group, 1536-dim extended feature, 2506 training images each

reactivity_delta_feature.probe: domain-matched (v7): jpeg_q50 for clean/spatial/noise/colorjitter, blur_s1.0 for jpeg - see domain_matched_probe_v7 below for why and the validation.
reactivity_delta_feature.validation_summary: cross-source generalization (leave-one-source-out): 0.72 (absolute embedding alone) -> 0.92 (delta alone, jpeg probe). Cross-generator generalization (leave-one-generator-out, Defactify TEST split): 0.909 -> 0.971 (combined). Survives being applied on top of an already-degraded (blurred) input: 0.816 -> 0.911 (combined, LOSO). Full production integration (all 5 domains, real training/eval pipeline, v6 universal jpeg_q50 probe): mean AUROC across 16-cell robustness grid 0.981 -> 0.997; generator-diagnostic pooled AUROC 0.940 -> 0.977.

domain_matched_probe_v7.what_changed: the 'jpeg' specialist's reactivity-delta now uses a blur_s1.0 probe instead of the universal jpeg_q50 probe the other 4 specialists still use - re-JPEG-probing an already-JPEG-degraded image is redundant by construction (same-family probe).
domain_matched_probe_v7.mechanism_confirmed: test_same_vs_cross_family_probe.py, tested on all 4 non-clean domains: jpeg (same-family jpeg_q50 +0.0004 vs cross-family blur_s1.0 +0.0078), spatial (same-family blur_s1.0 +0.0285 vs cross-family jpeg_q50 +0.0492), noise (same-family noise_s0.05 +0.0235 vs cross-family jpeg_q50 +0.0704), colorjitter (same-family colorjitter_up20 +0.0024 vs cross-family jpeg_q50 +0.0391). Cross-family beats same-family in every domain, no exceptions - confirms the mechanism generally, not just for the one case (jpeg) that motivated it. colorjitter shows near-total same-family redundancy (+0.0024) almost as extreme as jpeg's, meaning the current jpeg_q50-everywhere-except-jpeg production choice is validated across the entire domain set.
domain_matched_probe_v7.validated_at_full_scale: retrain_jpeg_specialist_domain_matched.py, full 2506-image training set, 443-image held-out test: domain-matched (blur probe) jpeg specialist AUROC=0.9953 vs the prior universal-probe (jpeg_q50) jpeg specialist AUROC=0.9938 on the SAME test images (+0.0015).
domain_matched_probe_v7.validated_on_ablation_subset: ablation_generalist_vs_domain_routing.py's production (domain-routed) column, which calls the live v7 production pipeline: clean=0.9982, noise=0.9942, jpeg=0.9949 on a 150-image test subsample per domain.
domain_matched_probe_v7.cost: a 3rd CLIP forward pass per image (base + jpeg_q50-probed + blur_s1.0-probed) instead of 2, since confidence-gated soft routing means every image needs every specialist's own probe delta, regardless of which domain it actually routes to.
domain_matched_probe_v7.IMPORTANT_caveat: the full 16-cell robustness grid has NOT been re-run end-to-end on v7 - an attempt got stuck/severely slow on this sandbox (repeated, unexplained CPU throughput degradation hit several jobs this session) and was killed rather than risk the submission deadline. v6's full-grid number (0.9974 mean AUROC, universal jpeg_q50 probe) remains the last fully end-to-end validated number; v7's jpeg-domain improvement is validated in isolation (full scale) and on a 3-domain ablation subset, but not yet reconfirmed holistically across all 16 cells. Given the isolated jpeg-domain gain is real and the other 4 domains are byte-for-byte unchanged from v6, a full-grid regression is unlikely but not proven.

domain_routing_ablation.question: does domain-specialist routing still add value now that reactivity-delta exists, or is it redundant with it?
domain_routing_ablation.method: ablation_generalist_vs_domain_routing.py: trained one pooled single generalist (no domain routing, universal jpeg_q50 probe only, 100 balanced training originals) and compared it against the live production (domain-routed) pipeline on the same 150 held-out test images, for clean/noise/jpeg domains.
domain_routing_ablation.result: generalist mean AUROC 0.9731 vs production (domain-routed) mean AUROC 0.9958 - a +0.0227 mean advantage for routing, present in every domain tested (clean +0.0146, noise +0.0173, jpeg +0.0362). Routing and reactivity-delta are complementary, not redundant: routing calibrates the decision boundary per degradation type (an appearance-space problem), reactivity-delta adds a content-origin signal that generalizes across degradation types (a different axis of information).

threshold_calibration.method: calibrate_threshold.py - same threshold_at_fpr/tpr_at_fpr methodology as byteprint/metrics.py, calibrated on pooled predictions across all 16 robustness-grid cells (7088 images, 2640 real) rather than a small dedicated split, for a more stable 1%-FPR quantile estimate. NOTE: calibrated on v6's predictions (robustness_per_image.json predates the v7 jpeg swap) - not yet recalibrated on v7.
threshold_calibration.usage: production_pipeline.calibrated_predict() applies this threshold for a binary decision; the required predict.py deliverable still reports raw probabilities per the brief's exact spec, unaffected by this.

bytesprint_comparable_metrics.description: computed for direct comparison against BYTEPRINT's own reporting conventions (byteprint/metrics.py's AUC/TPR@FPR/leave-one-generator-out) - see results_detector/summary_table.md
bytesprint_comparable_metrics.ela_connection: the reactivity-delta feature is conceptually related to classic Error Level Analysis (re-compress, compare) but relocated from pixel-space tampering-localization into CLIP embedding-space whole-image classification - notably, this project's Part 2 (pre-CLIP-pivot) tried literal pixel-level ELA-adjacent reactivity signals and they failed (best ~0.62 AUROC); the embedding-space version is what actually worked.

generator_diagnostic_final.description: held-out (Defactify TEST split, never trained on) per-generator accuracy, 60 images/class
generator_diagnostic_final.note: the reactivity-delta feature (v6) improved every single cell here over v5 (real 81.7%->88.3%, sd21 86.7%->96.7%, sdxl 98.3%->100%, sd3 91.7%->98.3%, dalle3 95.0%->98.3%, midjourney6 81.7%->96.7%; pooled AUROC 0.940->0.977) - the gain generalizes to unseen generators, not just the training-side robustness grid. Two specific hard, user-found real-world misses (a ChatGPT/DALL-E image of a complex NTU convocation scene, and a deliberately-blurred ChatGPT dog image) remain misses even after this fix (0.030 and 0.008 respectively) - these represent a content/style distribution gap (unusual real-world prompts vs. Defactify's simple COCO-caption-style training examples), a different problem than the generator-identity/robustness gaps this feature targets. See README 'Error analysis' and 'known_failure_examples/'.
